top_choice_rationale: P001 (Helpman and Melitz, B001) rests on a single identifiable discovery: productivity differences across firms drive selection into exporting and foreign investment, so trade reallocates activity across firms and adds a channel to the gains from trade. The core papers (Melitz 2003; Helpman, Melitz and Yeaple 2004) are more than twenty years old and have been tested and extended in firm-level data from many countries. The credited pair matches who supplied the selection model and the exports-versus-FDI sorting result. The main risk is the omission of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, and I judge it manageable if the citation is limited to selection and reallocation, makes no claim about settled welfare magnitudes, and the scientific background acknowledges the empirical precursors. If the Committee defined the discovery as the whole firm-level trade programme, the two-name award would be too narrow. P000 (no award) is ranked second because P001 is the only proposal on the slate and I judge it worthy.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile for Helpman or Melitz. My profile lists an SSE affiliation shared with committee colleagues Dreber Almenberg, Friberg and Strömberg. My market-design field and my listed co-authors are not credited on the proposal. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
